newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania gives more details on currency plan.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania gives more details on currency plan.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank on Thursday gave more details of its project to end the currency board system and change the litas-dollar peg.
Last week the bank announced it intended to end the currency board system in stages but to maintain the peg of four litas to one dollar.

Today it said in a statement the third stage of the project would start no sooner than 1999, and would involve shifting to a litas peg to the dollar and the planned European currency, the euro, or to a litas pegged only to the euro.
The litas-euro peg would be part of the bank's aim of tightening integration with Europe.
The bank's previous document had said the third stage of the plan could involve a link to the dollar and the mark and would start no earlier than 1998.

"It is best to start the third stage when the finance and currency markets have become relatively stable, the deposits of citizens and companies in banks are increasing constantly and when inflation does not exceed 0.5 to 0.8 percent per month for at least six months in a row," the central bank added.
This was the first mention of the level of inflation required for the currency changes to be launched.
A currency board prevents the central bank from using tools such as interest rate changes and intervention in the financial markets to steer policy.
The central bank's planned changes were a response to the new right-wing government's desire for a more flexible monetary policy.
